reuse.why: Replaces getDateWithSkippedWeekend with one shared applyWeekendRule in shared/schedules.ts and routes getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, the new getDatesInRange and schedule-template through it, reusing RSchedule and the months helpers.

duplication.why: The duplicated skipWeekend ternaries in schedule-template and getUpcomingDates are removed; drop-vs-move, holiday matching and the shift window are each defined once.

placement.why: Date-rule logic lives in shared/schedules.ts beside getNextDate, the handler sits with its siblings in server/schedules/app.ts, and the stored field name is fixed in rule-utils where the condition is built.

scope.why: Each edit serves one of the four steps; the rule-utils rename (weekendSolve to weekendSolveMode, plus frequency and holidays) is needed so getNextDate sees the full rule.

maintainability.why: A single nullable applyWeekendRule is easy to own; getUpcomingDates still uses a hard-coded count * 7 look-ahead instead of getShiftWindowDays, which can undercount with long holiday lists.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All occurrence-adjusting paths call applyWeekendRule; none keeps its own weekend check.

disguised_duplication.where: Prior copies are removed and replaced by calls to the shared function.

abstraction_drift.where: applyWeekendRule takes the rule object (holidays added as a field) and has the daily-drop branch, which is the rule itself; getShiftWindowDays takes holidays; getUpcomingDates sizes its look-ahead with a literal count * 7 rather than getShiftWindowDays but still adjusts through applyWeekendRule.
